title: Pour two tablets into a held bottle cap, then into a medicine cup
instruction: Give two tablets from the bottle without touching them: hold the bottle's cap in one hand and, with the other, tip two tablets from the bottle into it; tip any extra from the cap back into the bottle, then tip the two from the cap into the medicine cup. Leave the bottle standing and let go of everything.
context: Taking a counted dose from a stock bottle is a familiar household operation and a taught medication-handling method. One hand holds the cap level under the bottle while the other meters the pour by tilt, then the cap delivers exactly two tablets into the cup without a gripper touching them. Use inert placebo tablets for hardware reproduction; dimensions and the observed pour are documented in TECHNICAL.md.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top; arm bases at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305). (1) Stock bottle: a 120 cc white HDPE packer bottle with a 38-400 neck (50.5 mm across, 86.4 mm tall, 13.6 g, bore about 31 mm), with a paper label, standing open and upright at (0.360, -0.140). In it lie 30 round brown film-coated tablets, 10 mm across and about 5 mm thick, about 0.33 g each: over-the-counter 200 mg ibuprofen tablets (any brand whose label gives round, brown, 10 mm), used here as stand-ins for a dose of two; inert placebo tablets of the same size and shape serve equally and leave no drug residue on a shared rig. (2) Its cap: a white polypropylene push-down-and-turn child-resistant cap for a 38-400 neck (44.6 mm across, 17.2 mm tall, about 6 g; inside about 36 mm across and 13 mm deep), lying upside down, open side up, at (0.330, 0.050). (3) Medicine cup: an empty 1 oz graduated translucent polypropylene medicine cup (47.6 mm across the top, 28.6 mm across the bottom, 34.9 mm tall, about 1 g), standing loose at (0.400, 0.165). All three are loose on the bare table. Nothing else is on the table. The layout is the same in every trial. Both arms start at the ready pose with open grippers (pads 94 mm apart).
scoring: Counted at the end, with the trial video for the three rules that depend on what happened earlier. A tablet is in the bottle, the cap or the cup when its centre is inside that container; any other tablet (on the table, on the floor) is a stray. Zero for the whole trial, whatever happens later: (a) a tablet gets into the cup without first having lain in the cap for 0.25 s (poured straight from the bottle, for example); (b) a gripper is in contact with any one tablet for 0.25 s or more in total (pushed, pinched or carried; a tablet glancing off a finger is not counted); (c) for 0.25 s a tablet lies in the cap while the cap is not pinched by both fingertips of one gripper, or while it rests on the table (its lowest point less than 5 mm above the table), the bottle or the cup: whenever tablets are in the cap it has to be held in a hand and supported by nothing else. Otherwise: 1.0: exactly two tablets in the cup, the other 28 in the bottle, cup and bottle standing upright on the table (within 10 degrees). 0.7: exactly two in the cup and the cup standing, but up to three tablets left in the cap or stray, or the bottle not standing. 0.4: one or three tablets in the cup, the cup standing, at most three tablets left in the cap or stray. 0.2: nothing in the cup, exactly two tablets lying in the cap and no strays (the dose was counted out but not given). 0: anything else, including four or more tablets spilled. A score above 0.2 also needs every gripper's centre point at least 30 mm from the bottle, the cap and the cup, and everything still (under 1 mm of movement) for 1 s; until then the score is capped at 0.2. Where the cap ends up does not matter. In a real trial: count the tablets in the cup, the cap and on the table, pour the bottle out and count 28, and check (a) and (b) on the video.
reset_notes: Nothing is used up. Tip the cup, the cap and any strays back into the bottle and check it holds 30 whole tablets (replace chipped ones). With real ibuprofen, wear gloves for the reset and wipe the cap, the cup and the gripper pads afterwards. Stand the open bottle, the upside-down cap and the empty cup back on their three marks (tape rings on the table make this quick).
fidelity: PhysX, 240 Hz physics/20 Hz control. Tablets move by gravity and contact. Bottle/cup colliders use 16 staves: bottle walls 4 mm (real about 1 mm; bore 6 mm narrower), cup 2.5 mm. Smooth meshes are display only. No threads, cap liner or child-resistant mechanism. Convex tablets, friction 0.35; internal dimensions and masses estimated. No chipping or dust. Full assumptions: REFERENCE-SPEC.json and TECHNICAL.md.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (4,800 steps; it moved both arms about over the table, brushed the bottle and the cap (at most 1.2 N) without moving them, and never lifted or tipped anything, so all 30 tablets stayed in the bottle); demo: 1.0 (1,382 steps; the left hand pinched the cap 80 mm up, about 8.4 N on each fingertip, while the right tipped the bottle over it; one metered pour gave exactly two, both then tipped into the cup). Both runs on the final scene and scorer.
